name: Javier Anders
life: “I still remember my first bicycle's saddle held level by string.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Javier can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I borrowed a bicycle to deliver the last parcel. The parcel was a pair of cycling shoes.
appearance: Javier has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a washed violet jersey with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. In conversation Javier listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Javier treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Javier lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To deliver the final parcel on borrowed wheels.
family: Ines Baines is Javier’s aunt by marriage. Javier asks before bringing somebody along. Ines can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Two birthdays in one ward*, Ines says, “I am old enough that a surprise party feels like somebody rehearsing my funeral.”
connections: Jeff Jiang. They try the route by bicycle and by memories of the old flood road.

reactions.situation: A delivery customer refuses the late parcel
reactions.response: Javier checks with the intended recipient before leaving a late parcel.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Javier agrees on a sum and a date with the friend in private, keeping the arrangement out of family gossip.

reactions.response: Javier says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
